Keep the full original quadratic frame and its $K$ retained products. Suppose exactly three original products and three original additions are private, exactly two additions visible. After whole-current quadratic-carrier erasure and pruning, suppose the literal surviving inputs are
\[
 u=UV,\qquad S=C+u,\qquad g=AB,
\]
where $U,V,C,A,B$ are nonzero old homogeneous linear forms, $u,g$ are distinct original private products, $S$ is the unique hidden addition and $g$ is the first chronological visible high. The third product and second high are initially unrestricted. Then $\vc(G)\le K+2$, without retained optimality or an additional order of $S$ relative to the first cut. Original degrees, input occurrences, coefficients, fanout and low/context incidences remain fixed; repeated forms and wires are allowed.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Full-current carrier erasure protects the entire current value of every original minimum-degree-two node with an addition-only output path, including restored cuts, and erases its off-carrier occurrences wholly. It preserves the exact selected frame, $P_2,H,K$ and Boolean function, without asserting equality of every former higher polynomial term. All private products remain useful by Corollary~\ref{cor:threedeletedproducts} on one path arm and the two isolated edges. All private additions remain useful by Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums} on the four global missing edges. These uses precede every support simplification.

Let $f$ be the third private product. Positivity and its minimum degree at least two exclude any surviving contribution from $f$ into the stipulated homogeneous old wires $U,V,C,A,B$. It therefore cannot feed $u,S,g$. The hidden $S$ has degree one and cannot itself be a strict high. A selected degree-one trace through $S$ would select $C$ and make $S$ visible, contrary to its hidden status. Thus $S$ cannot feed a selected linear input, visible low or retained linear sum. There is no other hidden sum, and whole quadratic-carrier off-frame uses have been erased. Since $S$ is useful and the inputs of $u,g$ are fixed, it must feed $f$ directly as a literal input, possibly twice.

The useful $f$ must enter the selected output through a visible high. An equal-degree selected quadratic entry would retain it; a higher additive entry is a cut. It cannot feed the first high $g$ or its selected low without being retained or requiring an earlier cut. Neither the fixed $S$ nor another private product can carry it to a different high. Hence $f$ itself is the second visible high. Repeating $u$ or $g$ at that cut would leave $f$ without a useful exit. These arguments concern surviving original occurrences, not ancestry on erased branches.

The original $g$ has degree two, so its first selected low has degree one. Every retained degree-one boundary before $f$ has current value $D+\alpha g$, with nonzero old selected part $D$ and $\alpha\ge0$. Only the first insertion can affect such a trace. A raw-$u$ contribution would require another unequal cut; a selected $S$ contribution would make $S$ visible; the second cut cannot precede its own high. A boundary computed before the first cut has $\alpha=0$. The other literal input of $f$, besides $S$, is consequently raw $u$, raw $g$, raw $S$, or such a boundary:
\[
 f=Su,\qquad f=Sg,\qquad f=S^2,\qquad f=S(D+\alpha g).
\]
No retained quadratic carrier has a surviving off-frame use, and the private gate budget leaves no further source. This is the complete original input census, allowing every repetition and actual temporal restriction.

The exact two-occurrence frame, before substituting dependencies, is
\[
 P_2+gL+fM+qgf.
\]
Here $L$ is old homogeneous linear or zero. The context $M$ is old linear or zero for a degree-one second low, and scalar for a degree-two low. In the last two displayed $f$ cases the original $f$ has degree two, so $M$ is old linear or zero. A same-occurrence diagonal would put the nonzero square of its selected degree-one low in squarefree $P_2$; a degree-two low cannot feed a retained quadratic product. Thus all actual terms, including distinct-occurrence crosses, are retained. On $T$, the original $P_2$ vanishes and the globally safe support expression
\[
 Y=gL\vee fM\vee qgf
\]
must equal the target edge function. In the remaining support calculations, $q$ denotes its zero/positive flag; no original node or minimum degree is changed.

\emph{The three raw alternatives.}
If $f=Su$, then Booleanly $f=u$ and $Y=gL\vee uM\vee qgu$. The two independent old quadratics $g=AB,u=UV$ fit Lemma~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching}, with arbitrary affine contexts and its optional square coefficients zero. Restricting to one path arm and the two isolated edges gives the forbidden three-matching. This is a support application, not a deletion of one of the three original products.

If $f=Sg$, its support is $gS$, so
\[
 Y=g\bigl[L\vee S(M\vee q)\bigr].
\]
The factor $g$ has two linear clauses, and $S=C\vee UV$ has the two clauses $C\vee U,C\vee V$. For $q=0$, the product $SM$ has at most three affine clauses, and disjoining $L$ preserves that upper bound. For $q=1$ the bracket needs at most two. Hence $Y$ has at most five clauses, fewer than the target's eight.

For $f=S^2$, Booleanly $f=S$, so $Y=gL\vee SM\vee qgS$. If $C|_T=0$, then $S=u$ on $T$ and the same two-product matching lemma applies. Otherwise choose a target vertex $v\in\supp(C)$. Exactly four of the target's eight maximal independent sets contain $v$: choose either $x$ or both $y,z$, and one endpoint of each isolated edge. A valid affine linear clause can reject at most one maximal independent set, because the union of two distinct maximal independent sets contains an edge.

For $q=0$, distribute the disjunction of the three-clause product $gL$ and the three-clause product $SM$. Of at most nine clauses, six contain $C$ and are true on all four independent sets containing $v$. The other at most three clauses cannot reject all four sets. For $q=1$, use
\[
 gL\vee SM\vee gS=(g\vee M)(S\vee L)(g\vee S).
\]
The first factor has at most two clauses. The second has two and the third four, all six containing $C$. Again those four independent sets cannot all be rejected. Constants, repeated clauses and zero restricted forms only reduce the available capacity. Thus every raw alternative is impossible.

\emph{Full actual-context charges.}
We will use the following original-product observation. If a nonzero full direct context $F$ is contained in a three-vertex cover $Z$ of all four missing edges, mark the retained products reached by that insertion along selected linear paths. At least one is marked. Positivity puts each marked product's entire opposite old selected operand inside $\supp(F)$. Thus $Z$ covers every old edge supplied by all marked products. Add one star center for each unmarked original retained product. This covers $G$ with at most
\[
 (K-\#\{\hbox{marked products}\})+3\le K+2
\]
vertices, including every ambient old edge. No product of a rewritten support expression is charged. This applies to a full context that is an isolated target endpoint, or to a full context of the form $\{x,c\}$ with $c$ on an isolated edge.

\emph{Every nonraw coefficient case.}
Let $f=S(D+\alpha g)$ and let $\epsilon$ record whether $\alpha>0$. The actual contexts $L,M$ are old homogeneous linear or zero. Factor the support output as
\[
 Y=P\vee R,\qquad P=ABL,\qquad
 R=(C\vee UV)(D\vee\epsilon AB)(M\vee qAB).
\]
The first factor of $R$ has two linear clauses; each of the other two has at most two. Thus $R$ has at most six positive affine clauses for every pair of coefficient flags, with respective bounds $4,5,5,6$. No original wire or product is changed by this factorization.

The safe old cubic $P$ has at most one missing witness by Proposition~\ref{prop:oldfactors}. If it has none on $T$, then $R$ would realize the whole eight-clause target. If its single witness is a path arm, deleting that arm's other leaf leaves an induced three-matching supplied entirely by $R$, again requiring eight clauses. Therefore $P$ witnesses an isolated edge, say $ab$, and $R$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$.

If the full actual $L$ is a singleton, its $ab$ witness puts it at an endpoint of $ab$. The three-vertex cover formed by that endpoint, $x$ and one endpoint of $cd$ contains $L$, so the preceding original-product charge proves the desired bound.

Otherwise $L$ is nonsingleton. The full missing-cubic singleton certificate in Lemma~\ref{lem:commoncubic} makes one of $A,B$ a full singleton endpoint of $ab$. This uses the factor supplying the once-selected endpoint of a witnessing monomial, rather than an arbitrary choice among singleton factors. Set both $a,b$ to zero. Then $g=0$, and the other three target edges must be supplied by
\[
 (C\vee UV)DM=CDM\vee UVDM.
\]
Both terms are globally safe positive summands of the original $fM$ and retain their full old factors. The cubic has at most one missing witness; the quartic has at most two, forming an induced matching. Hence the quartic supplies one path arm and $cd$, while the cubic supplies the other arm. Relabel so the quartic witnesses $xy,cd$ and the cubic witnesses $xz$.

Full four-factor equality makes $U,V,D,M$ the four distinct two-point transversals of $xy,cd$, with no outside variable. Since $CDM$ witnesses $xz$ and $z$ is outside that quartet, both $D,M$ contain $x$. They are consequently the two transversals $\{x,c\},\{x,d\}$, and after exchanging $c,d$ the full actual $M$ is $\{x,c\}$. The three vertices $\{x,c,a\}$ cover all four global missing edges and contain $M$. The original-product charge again gives $\vc(G)\le K+2$. A zero $M$ could not supply the three remaining targets; repeated factors cannot evade the distinct-transversal equality case.

This exhausts every actual input of the otherwise unrestricted third product. The raw alternatives are impossible, and all nonraw alternatives satisfy the stated cover bound. Every charge retains the original selected products and all ambient old edges. No retained optimality, extra temporal order, longer-raw-input normalization or closure of the remaining numerical row is inferred.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The quadratic source as the first visible high]
\label{prop:sourcefirstunequalpreparation}
Let $G$ be finite, simple and $C_4$-free, and let a positive variable-input
circuit compute $P\in\operatorname{Sup}(G)$ with nonempty squarefree quadratic
support $H$. Suppose its four global missing edges have endpoint set $T$ with
$G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and $H[T]=\varnothing$. There are exactly three original
private multiplication nodes and three original private addition nodes,
exactly two of the latter visible. Preserve the full selected quadratic
frame, its arbitrary retained multiplication count $K$, and all original
minimum degrees, input occurrences, fanout, lows, contexts and incidences.
After whole-current-carrier erasure and off-frame pruning, suppose the sole
hidden addition has literal surviving inputs
\[
 u=UV,\qquad S=C+u,
\]
where $U,V,C$ are nonzero old homogeneous linear forms, singleton supports
allowed, and $u$ is an original private multiplication node. If the first
chronological visible high is the original node $u$ itself, the circuit
cannot supply the four missing witnesses. The other two private products and
the second visible high need no initial input restriction, and no further
order of $S$ relative to the first visible cut is assumed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Use whole-current-carrier erasure with its original ledger. At an off-frame
use it erases the entire current value of a protected quadratic carrier,
including a restored original degree-two cut-output carrier. It preserves
$P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean function; equality with the pre-erasure full
arithmetic polynomial is not asserted. All three useful private products
must survive: otherwise restricting to either path arm and the two isolated
edges contradicts the two-product matching obstruction of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching} and~\ref{lem:twoproductnormal}.
All three useful private additions must survive by
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. These are actual
frame-preserving reductions, before any Boolean factor simplification.

The first high $u$ has original minimum degree two, so its selected low has
degree one. Before the second high, every retained degree-one node has full
current support
\[
 D\vee\varepsilon u,\qquad\varepsilon\in\{0,1\},       \tag{1}
\]
where $D$ is its nonzero old selected linear value. This follows by induction
on the original retained linear nodes: variables are unaffected, retained
linear additions combine their selected linear parts and their $u$
coefficients, and only the first visible cut has yet inserted a high. A
positive variable-input multiplication cannot have minimum degree one. The
oldness of the full $D$ follows from its actual selected use: following its
retained linear path to a quadratic multiplication, any variable in the
nonzero opposite selected input is an $H$-neighbor of every variable of $D$.
This does not declare an arbitrary union of old forms to be old.

The hidden $S$ cannot enter a selected degree-one trace. Such a trace would
reach the unequal cut $S$, select its $C$ branch, and make that deleted
addition visible. Thus $S$ may be a raw private operand, but is not concealed
in a selected old linear part. Its full minimum degree remains one. Likewise,
a whole erased quadratic carrier supplies no additional off-frame boundary.
These facts hold whether $S$ is formed before or after the first visible cut.

We next derive the original two-product network rather than assume it.
Every useful remaining private product must enter the selected output through
a visible high. It cannot enter the literal $u=UV$ or $S=C+u$ through their
prescribed old homogeneous inputs. Entry through a selected quadratic low
would retain the product; entry through a retained degree-one node would
need a visible insertion. The first cut inserts only $u$. Therefore both
remaining products must feed the second visible high.

That high cannot be $S$, the first cut's current output, or any retained
linear value: each has nonzero minimum degree one and cannot be a strict
high over a nonzero variable-input low. It cannot be an off-frame quadratic
carrier, erased whole, or another private sum, since the sole hidden sum is
$S$. Consequently it is the later of the two remaining private products;
call it $f$, and call the other $v$. The node $v$ is an ancestor of $f$.
Their connecting path has no available intervening addition: $S$ depends
only on $C,u$, the first cut carries only $u$, and the second cut cannot be
an ancestor of its own high. A retained linear node cannot carry $v$ before
such a visible insertion, and an off-frame quadratic carrier is erased.
Thus the dependence is a raw product occurrence. Up to input order and
positive coefficients the literal skeleton is
\[
 v=XY,\quad f=vZ,\qquad\text{or}\qquad v=XY,\quad f=v^2. \tag{2}
\]
Every external boundary $X,Y,Z$ is raw $u$, raw $S=C+u$, or an actual value
(1). This exhausts the original nodes and includes repeated wires and raw
ancestors. In support only, the second skeleton has $f=v$ and hence two
external factor occurrences; the first has three. Both original product
nodes and their original minimum degrees remain recorded. No physical gate
count is inferred from this idempotence.

Since raw $S$ has support $C\vee u$, the resulting support list has two
forms. If a raw-$u$ boundary occurs, absorption gives
\[
 f=uF,\qquad F\text{ a product of at most two old factors},             \tag{3}
\]
where the empty product is allowed. Otherwise
\[
 f=\prod_{i=1}^{r}(A_i\vee\varepsilon_i u),\qquad 1\le r\le3,          \tag{4}
\]
with full nonzero old $A_i$ and listed occurrences retained even when their
supports coincide. Put $I=\{i:\varepsilon_i=1\}$ and $Q_0=\prod_iA_i$.
When $I\ne\varnothing$, put $F_0=\prod_{i\notin I}A_i$. Direct expansion
and absorption give
\[
 f=Q_0\quad(I=\varnothing),\qquad
 f=Q_0\vee uF_0\quad(I\ne\varnothing).                 \tag{5}
\]
Indeed the all-$u$ choice in the affected factors absorbs every other term
containing $u$. In the second case $F_0$ uses at most $r-1\le2$ of the same
listed old occurrences. Allowing $I$ empty only enlarges the list and will
also be covered.

Keep the two original visible occurrences separate in the frame. Their
exact private contribution, in support notation, is
\[
 Y=uL\vee fM\vee quf,                                  \tag{6}
\]
where $L$ is old homogeneous linear or zero, $M$ is its actual compatible old
homogeneous linear form, scalar or zero, and $q\in\{0,1\}$ records the
actual pair coefficient. A degree-two second low permits only a scalar
direct continuation and no cross, though the argument below even allows
$q=1$ then. Same-occurrence squares are absent: a degree-one low used on both
sides of a retained quadratic product would produce a positive diagonal
monomial in squarefree $P_2$, while a degree-two low cannot feed that product.
Fanout changes actual coefficients, not the occurrence labels. All terms in
(6) are safe, and on $T$ they must witness all four targets.

The induced target has eight maximal independent sets, so its edge function
needs at least eight positive CNF clauses. Each maximal independent set must
falsify a clause, and no clause can be false on two distinct such sets,
whose union contains an edge. A safe monotone function witnessing every
edge is exactly the edge function on this restriction.

If $M=0$, then $uf=uF$ for a product $F$ of at most three old factors,
by either (3) or (4). Hence $Y=u(L\vee qF)$ has at most five linear clauses,
including the two clauses $U,V$; empty products and zero contexts shorten
this bound. If (3) holds with $M\ne0$, then
\[
 Y=u\bigl[L\vee F(M\vee q)\bigr]
\]
also has at most five clauses: at most two clauses from the factors of $F$,
one from $M\vee q$, and two from $u$, with $L$ joined into each bracket
clause. This excludes every raw-$u$ case and every zero-$M$ case.

It remains to handle (4) with $M$ a nonzero old linear form or the scalar
$1$. Set $Q=Q_0M$, listing all $r$ old $A_i$ occurrences and, if $M$ is
linear, one additional occurrence for $M$. Thus $Q$ has between one and four
full old factors. Equation (6) has exactly the form
\[
 Y=Q\vee u(L\vee F),\qquad
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &q=0&q=1\\ \hline
 I=\varnothing&F=0&F=Q_0\\
 I\ne\varnothing&F=F_0M&F=F_0
\end{array}                                             \tag{7}
\]
where for the bottom-right entry $uF_0$ absorbs both $uQ_0$ and $uF_0M$.
Every nonzero $F$ in this table is a subproduct of the \emph{same listed
factor occurrences} of $Q$, using at most three. A scalar $M$ omits its
factor, and the empty product $1$ and repeated occurrences are permitted.
The first context $L$ is the actual old linear or zero context, and all
safety statements hold on full supports before restriction.
Proposition~\ref{prop:subproductcontext} therefore applies to (7), with its
quadratic high equal to the original $u=UV$, and excludes all four witnesses.

The inventory (2), the raw-$u$ case (3), and all flags in (7) exhaust the
original circuit under the stated hypotheses. No context type or original
minimum degree was recomputed after a Boolean simplification, and no extra
ordering of $S$ was imposed. This proves impossibility for every $K$, without
classifying a different first high or a longer hidden preparation.
\end{proof}

% Complete223 inserted after the separately completed full paired comparison.
\begin{proposition}[The full literal old-quadratic unequal preparation]
\label{prop:literalunequalpreparationcover}
Let a positive variable-input circuit compute $P\in\Sup(G)$, where $G$ is
finite, simple and four-cycle-free. Let its nonempty squarefree quadratic
support be $H$, and let the four global missing edges be $xy,xz,ab,cd$,
with $G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and $H[T]=\varnothing$ on their full endpoint
set $T$. Preserve the original selected quadratic frame and its $K$
retained products. After whole-current-carrier erasure and pruning,
suppose exactly three original products and three original additions are
private, exactly two additions visible, and the sole hidden addition has
literal surviving inputs
\[
 u=UV,\qquad S=C+u,
\]
where $u$ is an original private product and $U,V,C$ are full nonzero old
homogeneous linear forms. Then
\[
 \vc(G)\le K+2.
\]
The two visible highs and the other two private products are initially
unrestricted. No retained optimality or further order of $S$ relative to
the cuts is assumed. All original nodes, minimum degrees, input occurrences,
coefficients, fanout, selected lows and full contexts are retained;
repeated forms and wires are permitted.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use the original frame and whole-current protected-carrier erasure.
Every original minimum-degree-two carrier with an addition-only selected
continuation, including a restored cut output, keeps its entire current
value on that continuation and loses its entire off-frame use. This
preserves $P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean function, without claiming equality of
every earlier higher polynomial term. All three products remain useful by
Corollary~\ref{cor:threedeletedproducts} on one path arm and the two
isolated edges, and all three additions remain useful by
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. These actual reductions
precede all support identities below.

Before the first chronological visible cut, a retained degree-one boundary
is a full old homogeneous linear form: no earlier visible high has affected
it. Its oldness follows from its actual selected quadratic use and the
nonzero opposite selected operand. A selected trace through $S$ would
select $C$ and make $S$ visible, so $S$ is a separate raw boundary.
Off-frame quadratic carriers have been erased whole. The first high $g$
cannot be a retained linear signal or $S$, each of minimum degree one,
an erased quadratic carrier, or an unlisted private sum. Hence $g$ is an
original private product.

If $g=u$, Proposition~\ref{prop:sourcefirstunequalpreparation} excludes
it. Otherwise let $v$ denote the third private product, distinct from
$u,g$, without imposing its position relative to $g$. If raw $v$ is not
an input of $g$, it cannot enter indirectly: a retained linear path would
need an earlier visible insertion, the prescribed old inputs of $u,S$
cannot carry it, and a quadratic-carrier route has been erased. Thus the
complete literal input list for $g$ is an old linear form, raw $S$ or raw
$u$. Up to input order,
\[
 g=AB,\quad SA,\quad S^2,\quad uA,\quad uS,\quad u^2.
\]
The first two cases have the required bound by
Propositions~\ref{prop:independentquadraticfirst}
and~\ref{prop:earlierunequaloldfactor}; the others are impossible by
Propositions~\ref{prop:squaredunequalpreparation},
\ref{prop:rawcubicunequalpreparation} and~\ref{prop:unequalaliasfirst}.
Each cited result leaves the remaining product and second high
unrestricted and keeps the original degree and context data.

It remains that $g$ uses raw $v$. The node $v$ precedes $g$, while neither
can enter the fixed homogeneous inputs of $u$. Before the first cut,
$v$ has the same exhaustive old-linear/raw-$S$/raw-$u$ boundary list,
with actual temporal availability retained. Consequently
\[
 v=AB,\quad SA,\quad S^2,\quad uA,\quad uS,\quad u^2,
 \qquad
 g=vZ\quad\hbox{or}\quad g=v^2,
\]
where in the nonsquared case $Z$ is old linear, raw $S$ or raw $u$.
There is no intervening private sum: the only hidden one is fixed $S$;
retained linear sums before the first cut carry no private product;
whole quadratic off-frame values are erased. This derives the original
two-product network, including both raw $v$ input occurrences in $v^2$.

The useful $S$ must occur as a literal boundary of $v$ or $g$. It cannot
feed $u$ or its old inputs; no other private product or hidden sum remains
for a later exit. A selected linear trace would make $S$ visible, and
its minimum degree one prevents it from being a strict high. Without such
a boundary use it would be pruned, contrary to the original essentiality.
This is derived for the present case and imposes no extra order in the
previous cases.

The second high $h$ is one of $u,v,g$. A retained linear value or $S$
has minimum degree one. If the first selected low has degree one, its
restored cut output also has degree one and cannot be a strict high.
If that low has degree two, the restored output is a protected original
quadratic carrier with an addition-only selected continuation; its whole
off-frame use is erased. No other private sum or product remains. This
also excludes an unlisted high consisting of the first low plus $g$.

Keep the two original insertion occurrences distinct. Their exact private
contribution in support notation is
\[
 Y=gL\vee hM\vee qgh.
\]
The contexts have their actual old homogeneous linear/zero or scalar types.
In particular $h=u$ has original minimum degree two, so its selected low
has degree one and $M$ is old linear or zero. Same-occurrence squares
would give a positive diagonal from the selected degree-one low in
squarefree $P_2$; a degree-two low cannot feed a retained quadratic
multiplication. Thus all actual cross terms remain in $q$, even when
both insertion occurrences carry the same high. Affine linear contexts
may overestimate these types for clause bounds below, but an affine
mixture will never be treated as a listed old factor.

Every summand is globally safe, and on $T$ the old frame vanishes, so $Y$
must equal the target edge function. It needs at least eight positive CNF
clauses. Indeed its eight maximal independent sets choose either $x$ or
both $y,z$ and one endpoint of each isolated edge. Every such set must
falsify a clause; no clause can be false on two distinct maximal independent
sets, whose union contains an edge.

Each listed $v$ has at most three linear clauses: $AB$ has two;
$SA$ has three because $S=(C\vee U)(C\vee V)$; $S^2$ has the two
clauses of $S$; $uA$ has three; and $uS,u^2$ have the two clauses
$U,V$. A nonsquared $Z$ has at most two clauses. In the square case
use the support representation $g=v\cdot1$, retaining both original
$v$ input positions and $g$'s original minimum degree. Thus $g$ has
at most five clauses. If $h=g$, then $Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)$ has
at most six. If $h=v$, then $gv=g$ in support and
\[
 Y=v\bigl[M\vee Z(L\vee q)\bigr].
\]
The bracket has at most three clauses, including scalar and zero contexts,
so again at most six suffice. The effective $Z=1$ square case is shorter.
Both alternatives contradict the target.

It remains that $h=u$. The original $v/g$ network has at most three
external boundary occurrences; for $g=v^2$, support idempotence uses
$v$'s same two boundaries once, without deleting either original product.
If a boundary is actual raw $u$, every $S=C\vee u$ factor is absorbed
under $u$, leaving
\[
 g=uD\quad\hbox{in support},
\]
where $D$ is a product of at most two full old factors, with the empty
product allowed. Hence
\[
 Y=u\bigl[M\vee D(L\vee q)\bigr]
\]
has at most five clauses. This includes every repeated raw input and all
scalar/zero contexts.

Otherwise every external boundary is old linear or raw $S$, and at least
one is $S$ by the original essentiality above. Repeated $S$ factors have
the same Boolean support as $S$. Thus
\[
 g=SE=CE\vee uE\quad\hbox{in support},
\]
where $E$ is a product of at most two listed full old factors, possibly
$E=1$. No original wire or degree is identified. If $L=0$, then
$Y=u(M\vee qE)$ has at most four clauses. For nonzero $L$, retain
its actual old homogeneous linear or scalar type and normalize a positive
scalar to $1$ only in support. Put $Q=CEL$, listing $C$, the $E$
factors and, exactly when $L$ is linear, the $L$ occurrence. There are
between one and four nonzero full old factors. Exact expansion gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 q=0:&\quad Y=Q\vee u(M\vee EL),\\
 q=1:&\quad Y=Q\vee u(M\vee E).
\end{aligned}
\]
In the second line the actual mixed term $gu=uE$ absorbs $uEL$.
The respective subproducts $EL$ and $E$ use at most three and two of
those \emph{same listed occurrences} of $Q$; scalar $L$ adds none.
Empty subproducts and repeated factors are allowed. The actual outer
context $M$ is old linear or zero because the second high is $u=UV$.
All supports are globally safe by the exact original contribution.
Proposition~\ref{prop:subproductcontext} applies within each of its
stated hypotheses and excludes the four witnesses.

This exhausts both original highs and every remaining product input.
The last-product-first-high cases are impossible; the previously admitted
literal cases supply the required $K+2$ bound. The conclusion covers the
entire displayed preparation, with no first-high restriction. It does not
normalize a longer raw input to $S$, an affected input in place of the
literal old $C$, or another hidden placement. Every original gate count,
minimum degree and actual context was fixed before the support algebra.
\end{proof}

% Complete225 inserted after full mutual comparison; original staged text preserved.
\begin{proposition}[An affected input beside an old quadratic preparation]
\label{prop:affectedquadraticpreparationcover}
Let a positive variable-input circuit compute $P\in\Sup(G)$, with $G$ finite,
simple and four-cycle-free, nonempty squarefree quadratic support $H$, and
four global missing edges $xy,xz,ab,cd$. On their endpoints let
$G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and $H[T]=\varnothing$. Keep the full original quadratic
frame with arbitrary retained product count $K$. After whole-current-carrier
erasure and pruning, suppose exactly three original products and three
original additions are private, exactly two additions visible. Let $g$ be
the first visible high and let the sole hidden addition have literal inputs
\[
 S=R+u,\qquad u=UV,\qquad R=C+\beta g,\quad\beta>0.
\]
Here $U,V$ are full nonzero unaffected old homogeneous linear inputs to the
original product $u$. The actual degree-one boundary $R$ has nonzero old
selected part $C$; its displayed full value is obtained along actual
retained addition-only routes. The form $C$ alone need not be an available
circuit wire. Both visible highs and the other two original products are
initially unrestricted. Preserve every original degree, input occurrence,
coefficient, fanout, low/context identity and retained-product incidence.
Then
\[
 \vc(G)\le K+2.
\]
There is no retained optimality or additional chronological-order hypothesis.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use full-current-carrier erasure before any support identity: protect the
entire current value of every original minimum-degree-two carrier on an
addition-only output path, including restored cut outputs, and erase its
off-frame uses wholly. Every private product remains indispensable by
Corollary~\ref{cor:threedeletedproducts} on one path arm and the isolated
edges; every private addition remains indispensable by
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. The selected frame, $P_2,H,K$
and Boolean function stay fixed.

The degree-one boundary $R$ really carries the first insertion. Its actual
selected low $a$ therefore has degree one, and its selected addition-only
route gives $\supp(a)\subseteq\supp(C)$. A degree-two cut output could not
feed this trace, and its off-frame carrier use would be erased. Thus the
actual first direct context $L$ is old homogeneous linear or zero. This
conclusion is derived from the affected route, not added to the hypotheses.

Acyclicity puts $g$ before $R,S$. A hidden degree-one $S$ cannot be a strict
high; any selected linear trace through it would make that original unequal
sum visible. Hence it cannot enter a selected low or retained linear
boundary. With no other hidden sum or off-frame quadratic carrier, a useful
path from $S$ must enter a private product. That product is neither the
stipulated old-input $u$ nor the earlier $g$.

If $g=u$, the actual wires $R=C+\beta u$ and $S=R+u$ have identical Boolean
values. Replace every $S$ use by the existing $R$ wire. Their minimum degrees
and degree-one parts agree; a route from the hidden $S$ meets a multiplication
before reaching the selected frame, so the removed degree-two summand changes
only terms of degree at least three. The whole $P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean
function are preserved. Removing $S$ leaves at most three private products
and two additions, a contradiction. Therefore $u,g$ are distinct.

Let $f$ be the third product. Essentiality now forces a literal $S$ input to
$f$, possibly repeated, and $f$ is later than $S$. Its useful path must enter
the quadratic frame as a visible high: an equal-degree selected entry would
retain it, and a higher additive entry is a cut. It cannot return to $u,S,g$,
and no further private node exists. Thus $f$ itself is the second high.
Before $g$ there is no visible cut or hidden sum; only raw $u$ and unaffected
old linear boundaries are available. The complete original possibilities are
\[
 g=AB,\qquad g=uA,\qquad g=u*u,                         \tag{1}
\]
with full old $A,B$. In the first case $u,g$ are originally independent.
In the last case the original degree remains four despite its Boolean value.
The other input of $f$ is raw $u,g,S$, or an actual retained boundary
$D+\alpha g$ with nonzero old selected part $D$ and $\alpha\ge0$. A further
raw-$u$ insertion would need another visible cut; a selected $S$ trace would
make it visible; the second cut cannot precede its own high. Therefore
\[
 f=Su,\quad f=Sg,\quad f=S*S,\quad f=S(D+\alpha g).       \tag{2}
\]
These are original input lists, including repeated wires and actual temporal
availability. No new old $C$ wire has been supplied.

Expanding the exact two-occurrence frame before substituting dependencies
gives the globally safe contribution
\[
 Y=gL\vee fM\vee qgf,\qquad q\in\{0,1\}.                \tag{3}
\]
The context $M$ is actual old linear or zero for a degree-one second low,
and may be scalar for a degree-two low. In the last two cases of (2), the
original $f$ has degree two, so $M$ is old linear or zero. A same-occurrence
diagonal would put the nonzero square of a linear low into squarefree $P_2$;
a quadratic low cannot enter a retained quadratic product. The actual
mixed coefficient is retained. On $T$, $Y$ is the four-edge target and needs
eight positive affine CNF clauses, as does an induced three-matching. An
induced two-matching needs four.

We use Proposition~\ref{prop:oldfactors}, including full-support quartic
equality, and the once-endpoint singleton certificate in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:commoncubic}. A safe old quadratic or cubic has at most one
missing witness; a safe old quartic has at most two, an induced matching.
An old support meeting both path arms contains $x$, since otherwise its
$H$-center and $y,z,x$ form a four-cycle. The affine-context argument at the
start of Proposition~\ref{prop:bothaffectedrepeatedcubic} bounds three old
factors times an arbitrary affine context by two target witnesses. Two old
factors times such a context have at most three clauses, so cannot witness
two disjoint target edges; two witnesses must be the path arms.

We also retain the full-context product charge. If a nonzero full actual
$F\in\{L,M\}$ lies in a three-vertex cover $Z$ of all four global missing
edges, mark the original retained products reached by that insertion along
selected linear paths. At least one is marked. Every marked product's full
opposite old operand lies in $\supp(F)$ by positivity, so $Z$ covers all its
old edges. One old-star center per unmarked original product then covers
$G$ with at most $K-s+3\le K+2$ vertices, where $s\ge1$ is the number of
distinct marked products. This counts the full ambient graph and the
original products, including shared uses.

\emph{An independent quadratic first high.}
Let $g=AB$ and put $T_0=C\vee u$, so the actual $S$ has support $T_0\vee g$.
For $f=Su$, support $f=u$ makes (3) the two-independent-product matching
template $gL\vee uM\vee qgu$, impossible on one path arm and the isolated
edges by Lemma~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching}. This is a support application
with the actual affine contexts; it does not delete the original $f$.
For $f=Sg$, support $f=g$ gives $Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)$, at most three clauses.

For $f=S*S$, support $f=S$ gives
\[
 Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)\vee CM\vee uM.                     \tag{4}
\]
If $q=1$, this is the union of the three safe old quadratic or cubic terms
$g,CM,uM$, with at most three missing witnesses. If $q=0$, the safe function
$g(L\vee M)$ has three clauses and cannot witness two disjoint targets.
Since $CM,uM$ have at most one each, it must witness both path arms. Then
both $A,B$ contain $x$, so $g$ is true on $\{x\}$. The safe positive term
$gM$ forbids any of $a,b,c,d$ in the full $M$, since each makes an independent
pair with $x$. Consequently neither $CM$ nor $uM$ can witness either isolated
edge. This is a contradiction. Zero contexts only reduce the witnesses.

It remains to take $f=S(D+\alpha g)$ and let $\epsilon$ indicate $\alpha>0$.
The old contexts $L,M$ are linear or zero, and
\[
 \begin{split}
 Y&=P\vee Q,\qquad P=ABL,\\
 Q&=(T_0\vee g)(D\vee\epsilon g)(M\vee qg).
 \end{split}                                           \tag{5}
\]
The factor $T_0\vee g=C\vee UV\vee AB$ has the four clauses
$C\vee U\vee A$, $C\vee U\vee B$, $C\vee V\vee A$, $C\vee V\vee B$.
The other factors have at most $1+\epsilon$ and $1+q$ clauses. Thus $Q$ has
at most $6+\epsilon+q$, hence at most seven unless $\epsilon=q=1$.

In those three flag cases the safe old cubic $P$ has at most one missing
witness. None would force $Q$ to supply the eight-clause target. A sole
path-arm witness would force $Q$ to supply an induced three-matching after
deleting that arm's leaf, again impossible with seven clauses. Therefore
$P$ witnesses an isolated edge, say $ab$, and $Q$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$.
If the full $L$ is a singleton, its $ab$ witness puts it at an endpoint;
together with $x$ and an endpoint of $cd$ it is contained in a three-cover,
and the original-product charge proves the claim.

Otherwise $L$ is nonsingleton. In a cubic monomial of $ABL$ witnessing $ab$,
the once-chosen endpoint's factor is a full singleton. It must be $A$ or
$B$, at an endpoint of $ab$. Set $a=b=0$. Then $g=0$, and the other three
edges must be supplied by
\[
 T_0DM=CDM\vee UVDM.                                   \tag{6}
\]
Both are globally safe positive subfunctions of the original $fM$ with their
full old supports. The cubic has at most one witness; the quartic has at
most two, an induced matching. Thus the quartic witnesses $cd$ and one
path arm, say $xy$, and the cubic witnesses $xz$. Full quartic equality
makes $U,V,D,M$ the four distinct two-point transversals of $xy,cd$, without
outside vertices. Since $D,M$ also meet $xz$, both contain $x$. They are
therefore $\{x,c\},\{x,d\}$. After exchanging $c,d$, the full actual
$M=\{x,c\}$ lies in the three-cover $\{x,c,a\}$, and the original-product
charge again gives $\vc(G)\le K+2$. A zero $M$ cannot witness the three
edges; repeated factors cannot evade the distinct-transversal equality.

For the omitted flag pair $\epsilon=q=1$, absorption instead gives
\[
 Q=g\vee T_0DM,\qquad Y=g\vee T_0DM.                   \tag{7}
\]
Now $g$ itself is a globally safe old quadratic, with at most one missing
witness, and $T_0DM$ has at most four clauses. The same eight-clause arguments
exclude no witness or a sole path-arm witness for $g$. Thus $g$ witnesses
$ab$ and $T_0DM$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$. Safety makes the full supports $A,B$
disjoint, since a common vertex gives a singleton true assignment. If both
had size at least two, their complete cross rectangle would form a four-cycle
in $G$. One is therefore a full singleton at an endpoint of $ab$. Setting
$a=b=0$ kills $g$, leaving (6). Its full cubic/quartic allocation and actual
$M$ charge apply exactly as above. This handles the coefficient case in
which the crude count could reach eight; it is not included in the
seven-clause estimate.

\emph{A raw ancestor or repeated source.}
For $g=uA$ retain its actual old $A$. For the distinct original node
$g=u*u$, write $A=1$ only inside Boolean formulas. Its original degree four
and two input occurrences are unchanged; no unit gate is introduced. In
both cases $g$ implies $u$, so the actual affected $S$ has support $C\vee u$.
This does not replace its actual input $R$ by a new old wire.

For $f=Su$ the output is $u[AL\vee M\vee qA]$. Its bracket is
$(A\vee M)(L\vee M)$ for $q=0$, and $A\vee M$ for $q=1$; with $U,V$
at most four clauses suffice. For $f=Sg$, it is $g(L\vee M\vee q)$,
again at most four. For $f=S*S$, put $L'=L\vee q$ and $D_0=AL'\vee M$.
Since $CM$ implies $D_0$,
\[
 Y=uD_0\vee CM=(u\vee CM)D_0.
\]
The first factor has the four clauses $U\vee C,U\vee M,V\vee C,V\vee M$;
the second is $(A\vee M)(L'\vee M)$. At most six clauses suffice, including
$A=1$ and zero or scalar contexts. All raw alternatives are impossible.

For $f=S(B+\alpha g)$, with full old selected part $B$ and flag $\epsilon$,
the actual $M$ is old linear or zero. Using $ug=g$ gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 Y&=BCM\vee uF,\\
 F&=AL\vee BM\vee\epsilon AM\vee qAB\vee\epsilon qA.
 \end{split}                                           \tag{8}
\]
Every displayed term is a globally safe subfunction of the original output.
The exact four flag identities are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l}
\epsilon&q&F\\ \hline
0&0&(A\vee B)(A\vee M)(L\vee B)(L\vee M)\\
0&1&(A\vee B)(A\vee M)(B\vee L)\\
1&0&(A\vee B)(A\vee M)(L\vee M)\\
1&1&(A\vee B)(A\vee M).
\end{array}
\]
They include $A=1$, and show that $uF$ has at most six clauses. The safe old
cubic $BCM$ has at most one missing witness. If it has none, $uF$ would supply
the full eight-clause target; if it witnesses a path arm, $uF$ would supply
the induced three-matching after deleting its leaf. Thus $BCM$ witnesses
an isolated edge $ab$, and $uF$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$. The full old $U,V$
both meet the path arms and contain $x$.

If the full $B$ is a singleton, it is an endpoint of $ab$. Set $a=b=0$.
The remaining contribution is $g(L\vee\epsilon M\vee\epsilon q)$.
For old $A$, the three-old-factor affine bound gives at most two witnesses.
For $A=1$, it has at most three clauses and cannot even witness an induced
two-matching among the three remaining edges. Either way it cannot supply
$xy,xz,cd$. Its positive terms were already globally safe before restriction.
If instead the full $M$ is a singleton endpoint of $ab$, the same restriction
leaves $g(L\vee qB\vee\epsilon q)$ and the identical argument applies.
This includes positive constant contexts and zero summands.

Otherwise neither $B$ nor $M$ is a full singleton. In a witnessing cubic
monomial of $BCM$ on $ab$, the once-chosen endpoint must therefore be supplied
by $C$. Relabel so the full $C=\{a\}$ and $b\in B\cap M$. But the positive
safe term $uBM$ is true on the independent pair $\{x,b\}$, since both $U,V$
contain $x$. This final contradiction exhausts the singleton alternatives.
Thus every raw-ancestor and repeated-source case is impossible.

All actual input and coefficient cases have been covered. The possible
independent nonraw cases give the global full-context cover bound, with
original retained products charged once. Longer or affected raw sources,
other hidden placements, the remaining all-visible families and matching
attachments are not classified by this proposition.
\end{proof}

% Complete227 inserted after full mutual comparison; original stage preserved.
% The first selected low is renamed a_0 to distinguish it from target vertex a.
\begin{proposition}[A general raw source beside an affected hidden input]
\label{prop:generalaffectedpreparationcover}
Let a positive variable-input circuit compute $P\in\operatorname{Sup}(G)$,
where $G$ is finite, simple and four-cycle-free. Let its nonempty squarefree
quadratic support be $H$, and suppose the four global missing edges are
$xy,xz,ab,cd$, with $G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and $H[T]=\varnothing$ on their full
endpoint set $T$. Preserve the exact original selected quadratic frame and
its arbitrary retained multiplication count $K$. After whole-current-carrier
erasure and off-frame pruning, suppose exactly three original products and
three original additions are private, exactly two additions visible. Write
$c_1=a_0+g$ for the first visible occurrence. The sole hidden addition has
literal original inputs
\[
 S=R+u,\qquad R=C+\beta g,\qquad \beta>0,
\]
where $R$ is an actual retained degree-one boundary affected by $c_1$, with
full nonzero old homogeneous linear selected part $C$, and $u$ is any raw
original private-product output. The displayed value of $R$ is collected
along its actual retained addition-only routes; $C$ need not be an available
wire. Then
\[
 \vc(G)\le K+2.
\]
Neither visible high nor the original inputs, minimum degree or private
ancestry of $u$ are initially restricted further. All original node and
occurrence identities, minimum degrees, positive coefficients, fanout,
selected paths, lows, full contexts and retained-product incidences are kept.
Repeated wires and coincident Boolean values do not identify original nodes.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use whole-current-carrier erasure with its original ledger. Every original
minimum-degree-two carrier having an addition-only output path retains its
entire current value on that continuation, including restored cut outputs,
and loses its entire off-frame uses. This preserves $P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean
function, without claiming equality of all earlier higher terms. Every
private product is necessary by Lemmas~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching}
and~\ref{lem:twoproductnormal} on either path arm and the two isolated edges;
every private addition is necessary by
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. These are frame-preserving
necessities, not permission to delete gates after arbitrary support rewrites.

\emph{Original timing and last-product inputs.}
The actual degree-one affected route to $R$ forces the first selected low
$a_0$ to be nonzero old homogeneous linear and gives
$\varnothing\ne\operatorname{supp}(a_0)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(C)$.
A degree-two restored cut output cannot provide that surviving degree-one
route, and its whole off-frame carrier use is erased. Thus the first actual
direct context $L$ is old homogeneous linear or zero. The original $g$ and
$c_1$ precede $R$ and $S$.

The hidden $S$ has minimum degree one. It cannot be a strict high, and a
selected degree-one trace reaching it would select $R$ and make $S$ a visible
unequal cut. Consequently its useful route must enter a private product
before returning through a visible high. It cannot enter the earlier $g$ or
its own input $u$, and no further hidden sum or off-frame quadratic carrier
is available.

If $u=g$ as original nodes, $S=R+u$ is Booleanly equal to its existing input
$R$. Bypass $S$ by that wire. Both values have the same degree-one component
$C$ and minimum degree one. Every $S$-to-output route has a multiplication,
since otherwise a positive linear term would reach the output. The removed
$u$ term, of degree at least two, therefore changes output terms only in
degrees at least three. The selected frame, $P_2,H,K$ and Boolean function
are unchanged, while a private addition is removed. This contradicts
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}.

Hence $g,u$ are distinct. The third private product, say $f$, must receive
$S$ directly and must itself be the second visible high. It cannot return
to its earlier ancestors, and repeating an earlier high at the second cut
would leave $f$ with no useful exit. An equal-degree selected product entry
would retain $f$; a higher additive entry is a visible cut. Thus these are
three distinct original products, regardless of their Boolean values.

Every retained degree-one input available before $f$ has full value
$D+\delta g$, with $D$ nonzero full old homogeneous linear and $\delta\ge0$:
only the first insertion is earlier. An uninserted raw product would need
another cut, and an uncut $S$ trace would make $S$ visible. The oldness of
$D$ follows from its actual selected continuation to a quadratic product;
it is not asserted for an arbitrary union of old forms. If $\delta>0$, that
route also gives $\operatorname{supp}(a_0)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(D)$.
The exhaustive actual input list is therefore
\[
 f=Su,\qquad f=Sg,\qquad f=S^2,\qquad f=S(D+\delta g).
 \tag{1}
\]
It includes both input occurrences of a repeated wire and every compatible
temporal order. The second cut cannot precede its own high.

Keep the two original insertion occurrences independent in the frame.
Their exact private support contribution is
\[
 Y=gL\vee fM\vee qgf,\qquad q\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Here $M$ has its actual old-linear, scalar or zero type. In the last two
cases of (1), the original degree of $f$ is two, so its selected low has
degree one and $M$ is old linear or zero. Same-occurrence squares vanish:
a degree-one selected low squared in a retained product would put a
positive diagonal in squarefree $P_2$, while a degree-two low cannot feed
that product. The actual distinct-occurrence coefficient $q$ is retained.
Every positive support term used below is globally safe, and on $T$ the
frame vanishes, so $Y$ supplies all four targets. None of the support
identities below reassigns an original degree or a counted gate.

\emph{The arbitrary raw source.}
Suppose no surviving original path runs from $g$ to $u$. Then $u$ has no
earlier private-product input: $f$ is later, $g$ is not its ancestor, and
$S$ is its successor. No hidden addition is available before $u$. A genuine
$g$ coefficient in either retained degree-one input would give such a path,
so both coefficients are zero. Both actual inputs of $u$ are therefore
full unaffected old homogeneous linear forms. This is precisely the
old-source hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:affectedquadraticpreparationcover},
which gives the desired bound. No support-equivalent quadratic is substituted
for $u$ to invoke that proposition.

Otherwise $g$ is a surviving original ancestor of $u$. It has no earlier
private product, hidden sum or visible cut; its actual inputs are full
unaffected old homogeneous linear forms. Write $g=UV$. The complete actual
source types are
\[
 u=(A+\alpha g)(B+\gamma g),\qquad
 u=g(A+\alpha g),\qquad u=g^2,
 \tag{3}
\]
with full nonzero old selected parts $A,B$ and nonnegative coefficients.
For the first type, genuine ancestry requires $\alpha+\gamma>0$; its
zero--zero case is already covered by the preceding proposition. The
remaining two types have a literal raw-$g$ factor and hence Booleanly imply
$g$. Since the actual $R$ already contains $g$, they make $S=R+u$ Booleanly
$R$. The same existing-wire bypass used above preserves the degree-one
part, $P_2$ and the original frame and removes a private addition. It is
impossible, without changing the degree-three or degree-four source node.

Only the first type of (3) remains. Put $w=AB$ as a lower-support expression,
not as an additional original product. Every other term in the expansion
of $u$ implies $g$, already present in $R$ with positive coefficient.
Consequently
\[
 S=C\vee g\vee w,\qquad w=AB
 \tag{4}
\]
in support. This manufactures neither a $w$ wire nor a $C$ wire. The original
$u$ remains the same affected product with the same input occurrences and
minimum degree.

We use Proposition~\ref{prop:oldfactors}: safe old quadratics and cubics
have at most one missing witness, and a safe old quartic has at most two,
forming an induced matching. In the quartic equality case its four full
supports are exactly the four distinct two-point transversals. We also use
the once-selected-endpoint singleton certificate in
Lemma~\ref{lem:commoncubic}. Both the target and an induced three-matching
require eight positive CNF clauses; an induced two-matching requires four.
A safe subfunction witnessing all edges of such a restriction equals its
edge function there. Constants and zero restrictions only reduce upper
clause bounds.

\emph{All raw last inputs.}
For $f=Su$, support $f=u$ because $u$ is an actual summand of $S$. Equation
(2) becomes
\[
 Y=gL\vee uM\vee qgu,
 \qquad g=UV,\quad u=(A+\alpha g)(B+\gamma g).
\]
Restrict to one path arm and the two isolated edges. This is exactly the
forbidden template of Lemma~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching}, including one
positive coefficient after exchanging inputs, or two positive coefficients.
Restricted forms may be zero and the actual contexts affine, as allowed
there. The original third product $f$ is not deleted or relabelled by this
support argument.

For $f=Sg$, (4) gives $f=g$ in support and
$Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)$ has at most three affine linear clauses. It cannot
supply the eight-clause target, including scalar and zero contexts.

For $f=S^2$, its original degree is two, so $M$ is old linear or zero.
Equations (2) and (4) give
\[
 Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)\vee CM\vee wM.
 \tag{5}
\]
The product $wM=ABM$ is a safe old cubic support subfunction, since $AB$ is
the full quadratic lower part of the actual $u$ contribution. No extra
product is counted. If $q=1$, (5) is $g\vee CM\vee wM$; its three safe old
quadratic/cubic terms supply at most three missing witnesses.

If $q=0$, the safe term $g(L\vee M)$ has three linear clauses. It cannot
witness two disjoint target edges, whose induced two-matching needs four.
Thus it has at most two target witnesses, and two must be $xy,xz$. Each of
$CM,wM$ has at most one, so four witnesses force those two path arms into
the first term. An old full support meeting both arms contains $x$:
otherwise it contains $y,z$, and its old $H$-center gives a four-cycle with
$x$; the center cannot be $x$ because both arms are missing from $H$.
Therefore $U,V$ both contain $x$, and $g$ is true on $\{x\}$. Safety of the
positive term $gM$ excludes every isolated-edge endpoint from $M$, since
any would make it true on an independent pair with $x$. Neither $CM$ nor
$wM$ can then witness an isolated edge. This contradiction includes $M=0$.

\emph{All nonraw last inputs and mixed coefficients.}
Let $f=S(D+\delta g)$, let $\eta$ record whether $\delta>0$, and keep the
actual old linear or zero contexts $L,M$. The exact support factorization is
\[
 \begin{split}
 Y&=P\vee Q,\qquad P=gL=UVL,\\
 Q&=(C\vee AB\vee g)(D\vee\eta g)(M\vee qg).
 \end{split}
 \tag{6}
\]
The source coefficients $\alpha,\gamma$ disappear only because all their
additional terms imply the $g$ already in $R$; the actual source is unchanged.
When $\delta=0$, the second high has support $D(C\vee AB\vee g)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:quadraticlowerpartfirsthigh} applies exactly, including
its explicit allowance that $AB$ is a lower-support part rather than an
original multiplication node. It retains the actual frame, $K$, contexts,
degrees and incidences and gives $\vc(G)\le K+2$.

Take $\eta=1$. For $q=0$, the first factor of $Q$ has the four linear clauses
\[
 C\vee A\vee U,\quad C\vee A\vee V,\quad
 C\vee B\vee U,\quad C\vee B\vee V.
\]
The factor $D\vee g$ has at most two and $M$ at most one, so $Q$ has at
most seven. The safe old cubic $P$ has at most one missing witness. If it
has none, $Q$ supplies the whole eight-clause target. If it has one path-arm
witness, deleting that arm's leaf leaves an induced three-matching supplied
by $Q$, again impossible. We use the witnesses of $Q$ and its safety, not
an assertion that every higher-support term of $P$ vanishes under restriction.
Thus $P$ witnesses an isolated edge, say $ab$, and $Q$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$.

If the full actual $L$ is a singleton, its witness places it at an endpoint
of $ab$. The three-cover consisting of that endpoint, $x$ and an endpoint
of $cd$ contains $L$ and gives the original-product charge below. Otherwise
$L$ is nonsingleton. In a cubic monomial of $UVL$ witnessing $ab$, the old
factor supplying the once-selected endpoint is a full singleton. It is
therefore $U$ or $V$, at one endpoint of $ab$. Set $a=b=0$. Then $g$ vanishes
and the other three targets must be supplied by
\[
 (C\vee AB)DM=CDM\vee ABDM.
 \tag{7}
\]
These are positive safe support subfunctions of the original $fM$ with
full old factors. The cubic supplies at most one missing witness and the
quartic at most two forming an induced matching. Hence the quartic must
supply $cd$ and one path arm, and the cubic the other arm. Relabel so the
quartic supplies $xy,cd$ and the cubic $xz$. Full quartic equality confines
$A,B,D,M$ to the four distinct two-point transversals of $xy,cd$, with no
outside vertices. Since both $D,M$ also meet $xz$, and $z$ lies outside
that quartet, both contain $x$. They are thus $\{x,c\}$ and $\{x,d\}$ in
some order. Exchange $c,d$ so the full actual $M=\{x,c\}$. It lies in the
three-cover $\{x,c,a\}$ of all four global missing edges. Zero $M$ cannot
supply the required witnesses, and repeated supports cannot evade the
full distinct-transversal equality.

It remains $\eta=q=1$, which is not included in the seven-clause estimate.
Absorption in (6) gives
\[
 Y=g\vee(C\vee AB)DM,
 \tag{8}
\]
since $g$ also absorbs $gL$. The exposed $g$ is a safe old quadratic with
at most one witness; the other term has at most four clauses. No witness
or a sole path-arm witness for $g$ would force that term to supply an
eight-clause restriction. Thus $g$ witnesses an isolated edge $ab$, while
the other term supplies $xy,xz,cd$. Safety makes the full supports $U,V$
disjoint, since a common vertex would give a singleton true assignment.
If both had at least two vertices, their complete cross rectangle would
give a four-cycle. One is therefore a full singleton at an endpoint of
$ab$. Setting $a=b=0$ again leaves (7), and its complete cubic/quartic
allocation and full actual-context charge apply unchanged. This covers
every coefficient flag; none is included in an inapplicable clause bound.

\emph{The global original-product charge.}
In each use above a nonzero full individual actual context $F$, either $L$
or $M$, is contained in a three-vertex cover $Z$ of all four global missing
edges, and its associated selected low has degree one. It reaches at least
one original retained product along selected linear paths. Mark all such
products, each once. Positivity puts the entire opposite old selected
operand of each marked product inside $\operatorname{supp}(F)$. Hence $Z$
covers every old edge supplied by a marked product. Each unmarked original
quadratic product is an old star: squarefreeness makes its factor supports
disjoint, and four-cycle-freeness forces a singleton side. Choose one center
per unmarked product. These vertices cover all of $H$ and the four global
missing edges, including every ambient vertex outside $T$, using at most
\[
 K-\#\{\text{distinct marked products}\}+3\le K+2.
\]
Repeated paths, reused products, coefficients and repeated chosen centers
do not duplicate the charge. No product from a support factorization is
counted instead of an original retained node.

The old-source case, both raw-$g$ source types and every last-product input
have now been exhausted. Every alternative is impossible or gives the
claimed cover bound with the original $K$. This treats the entire genuinely
affected degree-one hidden-input family. It does not classify an unaffected
hidden input $R=C$ with a longer or affected raw source, the remaining
all-visible families or matching attachments, and it does not close the
numerical saving row.
\end{proof}

% Full author transcript inserted after the complete paired proof gate; original stage preserved.
\begin{proposition}[An unaffected hidden input with an ancestral raw source]
\label{prop:unaffectedancestralpreparation}
Let a positive variable-input circuit compute $P\in\Sup(G)$, where $G$ is
finite, simple and four-cycle-free. Its squarefree quadratic support $H$
is nonempty, and its four global missing edges are $xy,xz,ab,cd$. On their
full endpoint set $T$, assume $G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and $H[T]=\varnothing$.
Preserve the exact original selected quadratic frame and its arbitrary
retained multiplication count $K$. After whole-current-carrier erasure
and off-frame pruning, suppose exactly three original products and three
original additions are private, exactly two additions visible. Write
$c_1=a_0+g$ for the first visible occurrence. The unique hidden addition
has the literal original inputs
\[
 S=C+u,
\]
where $C$ is an actual full unaffected nonzero old homogeneous linear
input wire, and $u$ is a raw original private-product output of minimum
degree at least two. Suppose $u$ is a proper descendant of the original
first visible high $g$ in the surviving original private network.
Then
\[
 \vc(G)\le K+2.
\]
No further restriction is imposed on the original operands, minimum degree
or coefficient pattern of $u$, or on the second visible high. All original
nodes, input and insertion occurrences, minimum degrees, coefficients,
fanout, selected lows and paths, full contexts and retained-product
incidences remain fixed. Repeated inputs and all compatible scalar or zero
contexts are allowed. No retained optimality or hidden-input coefficient
normalization is assumed.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
We work in the given original ledger after the general whole-current-carrier
erasure: protected selected continuations keep the entire current carrier
value, and off-frame uses lose that entire value, not merely its quadratic
part. This preserves $P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean function without asserting
equality of all higher terms. Every private product is necessary by
Lemmas~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching} and~\ref{lem:twoproductnormal}, restricted
to either path arm and the two isolated edges; every private addition is
necessary by Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. These necessities
concern actual frame-preserving reductions.

\emph{Complete original inventory.}
The distinct original products $g,u$ precede $S$. The first insertion
$c_1$ may precede or follow $S$; no extra cut order is assumed. A positive affected coefficient in the original source $u$ forces $c_1$
before $u$ and hence before $S$; a coefficient in the last product instead
requires only its actual availability there.

The hidden $S$ has minimum degree one and cannot be a strict high. A
selected degree-one trace reaching it would make its original unequal
addition visible. Its useful route must therefore enter a private product
before returning to the selected frame through a visible high. It cannot
return to $g$ or $u$. The third private product, call it $f$, is consequently
after $S$, receives $S$ literally, and is the second visible high. There
is no further private addition or product for another useful exit. An
equal-degree retained product would select a trace through $S$, again
contrary to hiddenness. Thus $g,u,f$ exhaust the distinct original products,
even if some Boolean values happen to coincide.

Since $g$ is earlier than the other products and the hidden sum, its actual
inputs are full unaffected old homogeneous linear wires $U,V$:
$g=UV$ is an original degree-two product. Its first selected low $a_0$ is
nonzero old homogeneous linear, and its individual direct context $L$ is
old homogeneous linear or zero, never a positive scalar.
Before the second cut, a retained degree-one boundary has the full value
$A+\alpha g$, where $A$ is a full nonzero old selected part and
$\alpha\ge0$. Only $c_1$ can affect such a boundary. An uninserted raw
product or uncut $S$ cannot occur on its selected trace without another
visible occurrence. A positive coefficient includes the first low in the
selected part; no such inclusion in the unaffected $C$ is assumed.
Oldness follows from that boundary's selected continuation to a quadratic
product, not from closure under arbitrary unions.

The full original source list is therefore
\[
 u=(A+\alpha g)(B+\gamma g),\quad \alpha+\gamma>0;
 \qquad u=g(A+\alpha g),\quad \alpha\ge0;
 \qquad u=g^2.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The zero--zero first case cannot have the assumed surviving ancestry.
Input reversal and repeated wires are permitted. The other literal input
of $f$ is exactly one of $u,g,S,D+\delta g$, with $D$ a full nonzero old
selected part and $\delta\ge0$. Thus
\[
 f=Su,\qquad Sg,\qquad S^2,\qquad S(D+\delta g).       \tag{2}
\]
These are actual operand forms. They do not supply a separate wire for
an old selected part $A,B,D$.

Keep the two original insertion occurrences separate. Their exact private
support contribution is
\[
 Y=gL\vee fM\vee qgf,\qquad q\in\{0,1\}.              \tag{3}
\]
Here $M$ retains its actual old-linear, scalar or zero type. For the last
two cases in (2), the original minimum degree of $f$ is two, so its selected
low has degree one and $M$ is old linear or zero. The raw cases retain
all compatible affine contexts. A same-occurrence diagonal would put a
positive square of a nonzero linear low into squarefree $P_2$; a quadratic
low cannot enter a retained quadratic multiplication. The actual
distinct-occurrence coefficient $q$ is kept. All expanded positive
subfunctions of (3) are globally safe and together witness the four
targets on $T$.

\emph{An actual deletion when the source is Booleanly $g$.}
For $u=g^2$, or $u=g(A+\alpha g)$ with $\alpha>0$, the full Boolean support
of $u$ equals that of $g$. Replace every use of the actual $u$ output by the
existing earlier wire $g$, and remove $u$. This removes an original node
rather than relabeling its degree. Every output use of $u$ must pass through
$f$, via $S$ or as the other raw input: there is no visible insertion of
$u$, selected trace accepting it, or remaining off-frame carrier use.
Every replaced contribution therefore acquires a positive-degree factor
before the output. The replacement $g$ has degree two, so all new output
contributions still have degree at least three. Hence $P_2,H$ and the
protected selected frame, including $K$, are unchanged. The linear part
of $S$ remains exactly $C$. A raw $f=Su$ now has minimum degree three,
still above either possible original selected-low degree; a square or
nonraw $f$ keeps minimum degree two. Boolean support is unchanged, and at
most two private products remain, contradicting the cited matching
obstruction. Thus the remaining source types are the raw cubic $u=gA$
with unaffected old $A$, and the single-affected or both-affected
minimum-degree-two forms in (1).

\emph{A clause argument and the full-context alternatives.}
Proposition~\ref{prop:oldfactors} bounds old quadratics and cubics by one
missing witness, and old quartics by two, necessarily an induced matching.
At quartic equality the full supports are the four distinct two-point
transversals, with no outside vertices. We also use the full singleton
certificate of Lemma~\ref{lem:commoncubic}. The induced path target and an
induced three-matching each require eight positive affine linear CNF
clauses; an induced two-matching requires four. These follow from their
maximal independent sets, each requiring a different falsified valid
clause. Zero factors and constant clauses only decrease an upper bound.

Suppose $Y=P_0\vee Q$ with $P_0=gL=UVL$ safe and $Q$ safe with at most
seven such clauses. The old cubic $P_0$ has at most one target witness.
If it has none, $Q$ supplies the whole eight-clause target. If its only
witness is a path arm, deleting that arm's leaf leaves an induced
three-matching supplied by $Q$, also impossible. Here safety and all
edge witnesses give the restricted edge function; it is unnecessary to
assert that all higher terms of $P_0$ vanish. Thus $P_0$ witnesses an
isolated edge, say $ab$, and $Q$ supplies $xy,xz,cd$.

In a witnessing monomial of $UVL$, the old factor supplying the once-chosen
endpoint has full singleton support. If the full actual $L$ is a singleton,
it is an endpoint of $ab$ and lies in a three-cover of all four global
missing edges, together with $x$ and one endpoint of $cd$. This gives the
original-product charge below. Otherwise $U$ or $V$ is a full singleton
at an endpoint of $ab$. Setting $a=b=0$ kills all of $g$.

Several branches below then leave $0,CM,CDM$, or $CM\vee ABM$, with old
linear $M$ whenever one of the latter expressions occurs. These have
respectively at most $0,1,1,2$ target witnesses and cannot supply
$xy,xz,cd$. The remaining common possibility is
\[
 CDM\vee ABDM.                                     \tag{4}
\]
Its safe old cubic has at most one witness and its old quartic at most two.
Three required targets force the quartic to supply $cd$ and one path arm,
and the cubic the other. Relabel so the quartic supplies $xy,cd$ and the
cubic supplies $xz$. Full quartic equality makes $A,B,D,M$ the four
distinct transversals of $xy,cd$. Since $D,M$ also meet $xz$, and $z$ is
outside that quartet, both contain $x$. They are $\{x,c\}$ and $\{x,d\}$.
After exchanging $c,d$, the full actual $M=\{x,c\}$ lies in the three-cover
$\{x,c,a\}$. Every application of this alternative below has original
minimum degree two for $f$, so $M$ is the context of a degree-one selected
low and supplies the same global charge. Full-support equality, not a
restricted-only context, is used here.

\emph{The raw cubic source $u=gA$.}
Now $S=C\vee UVA$ has at most three linear clauses. For $f=Su$ the support
is $f=u$, and
\[
 Q=UVA(M\vee q)
\]
has at most four affine clauses. For $f=Sg$, it is
$Q=g(C\vee A)(M\vee q)$, again at most four; affine $M$ is fully allowed.
In both cases the preceding argument either charges a full singleton $L$
or kills $g$ and all of $Q$, a contradiction.
For $f=S^2$, $M$ is old linear or zero and
$Q=(C\vee UVA)(M\vee qg)$ has at most five clauses. Killing $g$ leaves $CM$,
too few witnesses. Finally, for $f=S(D+\delta g)$, let $\eta$ indicate
$\delta>0$. Then
\[
 Q=(C\vee UVA)(D\vee\eta g)(M\vee qg)
\]
has at most $3+(1+\eta)+(1+q)\le7$ clauses. Killing $g$ leaves $CDM$,
again impossible. Thus every raw-cubic branch is impossible or supplies
the full $L$ charge, including all zero contexts and coefficient flags.

\emph{A single-affected source.}
Exchange its actual inputs if needed and write $u=A(B+\gamma g)$ with
$\gamma>0$. Its minimum degree is two, and
\[
 S=C\vee AB\vee Ag
   =(C\vee A)(C\vee B\vee U)(C\vee B\vee V).          \tag{5}
\]
This exact three-clause identity creates no $AB$ gate.
For $f=Su$, support $f=u$ makes (3) precisely the single-affected
two-product matching template of Lemma~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching}.
Restricting to a path arm and the two isolated edges contradicts it.
Restricted forms may be zero and contexts affine, as that lemma permits;
the physical $f$ gate has not been deleted.
For $f=Sg$, support $f=g(C\vee A)$ gives the same four-clause charge-or-kill
argument as above.
For $f=S^2$, $Q=S(M\vee qg)$ has at most five clauses; killing $g$ leaves
$CM\vee ABM$, too few witnesses.
For $f=S(D+\delta g)$,
\[
 Q=S(D\vee\eta g)(M\vee qg)
\]
has at most seven clauses for every $\eta,q$, including $\eta=q=1$.
The common argument charges a singleton $L$, or killing $g$ leaves exactly
(4), whose full quartic allocation charges the actual $M$. This treats
every single-affected source branch.

\emph{Both source inputs affected.}
For $u=(A+\alpha g)(B+\gamma g)$ with $\alpha,\gamma>0$,
\[
 u=AB\vee g,\qquad S=C\vee AB\vee g                 \tag{6}
\]
in support. Its original minimum degree remains two; $AB$ is only its
lower old support part. The actual $C$ remains unaffected, with no
first-low containment imposed.

For $f=Su$, (3) is the both-affected two-product matching template and is
forbidden on a path arm and the two isolated edges. This is a support
obstruction, with no physical gate removal. For $f=Sg$, support $f=g$
gives $Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)$ with at most three affine clauses.

For $f=S^2$, $M$ is old linear or zero and
\[
 Y=g(L\vee M\vee q)\vee CM\vee ABM.                 \tag{7}
\]
If $q=1$, the safe old quadratic $g$ and the old quadratic/cubic terms
$CM,ABM$ supply at most three targets. If $q=0$, the three-clause
$g(L\vee M)$ cannot witness two disjoint targets. It has at most two;
if two, they are the path arms. Since the other terms have at most one
each, four witnesses force both path arms into that first term.
Then full old $U,V$ contain $x$: otherwise a factor meeting both arms
contains $y,z$, whose $H$-center forms a four-cycle with $x$. The center
cannot be $x$ because the arms are missing from $H$. Thus $g(\{x\})=1$,
and safety of $gM$ excludes every isolated endpoint from $M$. Neither
$CM$ nor $ABM$ can then supply an isolated edge, a contradiction also
covering $M=0$.

It remains to treat $f=S(D+\delta g)$. With $M$ old linear or zero,
\[
 Y=P_0\vee Q,\qquad
 Q=(C\vee AB\vee g)(D\vee\eta g)(M\vee qg).          \tag{8}
\]
If $\delta=0$, this is exactly
Proposition~\ref{prop:quadraticlowerpartfirsthigh}, with
$f=D(C\vee AB\vee g)$. That proposition expressly permits $AB$ as a
lower-support part. The actual old forms, original frame, $K$, degrees
and contexts meet its hypotheses; no available wire for a selected part
is supplied. It gives $K+2$ without requiring an affected hidden input.

If $\eta=1,q=0$, the first factor in (8) has four clauses,
$C\vee A\vee U$, $C\vee A\vee V$, $C\vee B\vee U$ and $C\vee B\vee V$.
The second has at most two and $M$ at most one. Thus $Q$ has at most seven
clauses. The common argument gives a full singleton $L$ charge or, after
killing $g$, the full actual $M$ charge from (4).
Repeated old supports cannot evade the required distinct-transversal
equality, and zero $M$ cannot supply the required witnesses.

The flag $\eta=q=1$ is separate; no seven-clause estimate is asserted.
Absorption gives
\[
 Y=g\vee(C\vee AB)DM.                              \tag{9}
\]
The second term has at most four clauses. The exposed safe old quadratic
$g$ has at most one missing witness. If it has none, or only a path arm,
the other term supplies respectively the eight-clause target or an
induced three-matching after deleting that arm's leaf. Hence $g$ witnesses
an isolated edge $ab$, and the other term supplies $xy,xz,cd$.
Safety makes the full $U,V$ disjoint. If both had at least two vertices,
their complete cross rectangle would be a four-cycle. One is therefore a
full singleton at an endpoint of $ab$. Setting $a=b=0$ kills $g$ and
leaves (4), whose full allocation again supplies the actual $M$ charge.
All flags in the both-affected case are now covered without importing
an affected-$C$ hypothesis from a different theorem.

\emph{The global original-product charge.}
In every surviving branch, a nonzero full individual actual context $F$,
either $L$ or $M$, lies in a three-vertex cover $Z$ of all four global
missing edges. Its associated selected low has degree one: for $L$ this
follows from the original old quadratic $g$, and each charge using $M$
occurs for an original minimum-degree-two $f$.
Follow the insertion along all selected degree-one continuations to the
first retained quadratic product on each path. At least one original
product is reached, since a nonzero linear direct context at a selected
quadratic output requires a multiplication. Mark the distinct products
reached, each once. Positivity places each marked product's full opposite
old selected operand inside $\operatorname{supp}(F)$. Thus $Z$ covers
every old edge supplied by each marked original product.

Each unmarked retained quadratic product is a star in $H$: squarefree
$P_2$ makes its selected supports disjoint, and four-cycle-freeness prevents
both sides from being nonsingleton. Choose a center for each unmarked
product. These centers and $Z$ cover all of $H$, including arbitrary
ambient vertices outside $T$, and all four global missing edges. With
$s\ge1$ distinct marked products, their number is at most
\[
 K-s+3\le K+2.
\]
Sharing, repeated paths and repeated centers only decrease the count.
No displayed factor, lower part $AB$ or restricted context is charged as
an original retained multiplication.
The complete source list (1) and last-input list (2) are exhausted.
The conclusion is only the stated proper-ancestral-source branch with
the actual unaffected input $C$; it gives no classification for a source
equal to $g$, a non-descendant source, other hidden orders, all-visible
patterns, matching attachments or the numerical saving row.
\end{proof}

% Full author transcript inserted after the complete paired proof gate; original stage preserved.
\begin{proposition}[An unaffected hidden input whose source is the first high]
\label{prop:sourceisfirsthigh}
Let a positive variable-input circuit compute $P\in\Sup(G)$ for a finite,
simple, four-cycle-free graph $G$. Its squarefree quadratic support $H$
is nonempty. The four global missing edges are $xy,xz,ab,cd$, and their
full endpoint set $T$ satisfies $G[T]=P_3\sqcup2K_2$ and
$H[T]=\varnothing$. Preserve the exact original selected quadratic frame
and its arbitrary retained multiplication count $K$. After
whole-current-carrier erasure and off-frame pruning, suppose exactly
three original products and three original additions are private, exactly
two additions visible. The unique hidden addition has literal inputs
\[
 S=C+u,
\]
where $C$ is an actual full unaffected nonzero old homogeneous linear
input wire, and $u$ is a raw original private-product output.
Suppose the first visible high is the same original product node $u$.
Then
\[
 \vc(G)\le K+2.
\]
The source's original inputs, minimum degree and other private ancestors,
and the second visible high, are initially unrestricted. No additional
order between the first insertion occurrence and $S$ is imposed.
Every original node, input and insertion occurrence, minimum degree,
coefficient, fanout, selected low and path, full context and retained-product
incidence is kept. Repeated inputs, coincident Boolean values, all
compatible scalar or zero contexts, and all actual cross coefficients
retain their original meanings. No retained optimality is assumed.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Write $g=u$ for the same original source node. Thus $g$ precedes $S=C+g$,
but its first insertion $c_1=a_0+g$ may precede or follow $S$.
Use only whole-current-carrier erasure with the protected selected frame:
the entire current carrier value is removed on off-frame uses, preserving
$P_2,H,K$ and the Boolean function. Private-product necessity follows from
Lemmas~\ref{lem:twoproductmatching} and~\ref{lem:twoproductnormal} on either
path arm and the isolated edges; private-addition necessity follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:threeproductstwosums}. These are necessities for
actual frame-preserving reductions.

\emph{The full source and last-product inventory.}
The degree-one hidden $S$ cannot be a strict high, or lie on a selected
degree-one trace without becoming visible. A useful $S$ route must traverse
a private product before returning through a visible high. It cannot
return to its earlier source $g$. It cannot enter the first occurrence's
high, which is that fixed earlier node; entry through a selected low would
retain a trace through $S$ or a private product, contrary to the frame.
Hence a product after $S$ reaches the second visible high.

If $g$ has actual full unaffected old homogeneous linear inputs,
Proposition~\ref{prop:literalunequalpreparationcover} applies exactly to
$S=C+g$ and gives $K+2$, with the other products and highs unrestricted.
This invocation requires actual old input wires, not an old quadratic
support identity.
Otherwise $g$ has an earlier private-product ancestor $t$. Together with
a product after $S$, these nodes exhaust the budget. No hidden sum or
visible insertion can precede the first high node $g$: both $S$ and $c_1$
use it. Consequently $t=UV$ has two actual full unaffected old homogeneous
linear inputs. Every input of $g$ is raw $t$ or an unaffected old linear
